title: Maximal geometric branch locus and its one-step blowup
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover), let $B\subset X$ be a normal crossings divisor, and let $D\subset B$ be a nonempty reduced union of irreducible components. A normal crossings divisor means a reduced effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor) [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] which, etale locally [def-weil-etale-morphism], has equation $t_1\cdots t_r=0$ for distinct members of a regular system of parameters; a regular system of parameters in a regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is a set of $\dim R$ elements generating $\mathfrak m$. A geometric point is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed; in an etale chart through it, its geometric prime is the prime of the chart ring underlying its image. Define $b_D(\bar x)$ to be the number of coordinate factors for $D$ whose images lie in that geometric prime (equivalently, the number of local branches of $D$ through $\bar x$). These numbers have a finite maximum $m\geq1$. The locus where $b_D=m$, endowed with its reduced closed subscheme structure $M$, is a nonempty regular closed subscheme of $X$. Etale locally at each point of $M$ one can choose the above parameters so that $D=V(t_1\cdots t_m)$, $B=V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ with $m\leq r$, and $M=V(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$. Let $b:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_M(X)\to X$ be the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] and $D^+$ the strict transform of $D$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Then $D^+$ is empty or a normal crossings divisor and $b_{D^+}(\bar y)\leq m-1$ at every geometric point of $X^+$.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.6 and 4.1.8, printed p. 118; local computation in 4.2.8--4.2.9, printed pp. 120--121. Geometric branches are used to make the normalization-fibre count precise.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-nc-subboundary-branch-atlas], the branch numbers are bounded and all upper level sets are closed. Nonempty $D$ supplies a positive branch value, so choose the largest attained value $m\ge1$. Then $T=\{b_D\ge m\}=\{b_D=m\}$ is nonempty and closed; outside $T$ the count is less than $m$. A pointed chart of that lemma at $x\in T$ has exactly $m$ factors for $D$, with $D_W=V(t_1\cdots t_m)$ and $B_W=V(t_1\cdots t_r)$.

In these charts [lem-trf-nc-coordinate-max-stratum] identifies $e^{-1}(T)$ with $V(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$, regular and reduced. These regular reduced models exist above every point of $T$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-reduced-regular-center] to $T$: its reduced closed structure $M$ is regular and pulls back to exactly that coordinate intersection, as a closed subscheme. Its quasi-coherent defining ideal is of finite type, since $X$ is locally Noetherian. This proves all claimed equations for $B,D,M$.

source.place: VIII 4.1.8, printed p. 118: the reduced coordinate center.

proof.text: Each etale chart $e:W\to X$ is flat [def-weil-etale-morphism], so $p:D\times_XW\to D$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. A point is component-generic iff it has no proper generalization, by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover, lem-sc-scheme-sober] and maximality of components. If $z$ is component-generic and $d$ generalizes $p(z)$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] gives a generalization $z'$ of $z$ with $p(z')=d$; so $z'=z$ and $d=p(z)$. This is the generic-point hypothesis of [lem-trf-strict-transform-flat-etale-base-change]; apply it to the finite-type ideal of $M$: $W\times_XX^+\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{M_W}(W)$ canonically, carrying the pulled-back $D^+$ to the strict transform of $D_W$ scheme-theoretically.

source.place: VIII 4.1.8, etale localization; strict-transform closure comparison as in Stacks 081I.

proof.text: Each affine chart $W$ of steps 1--2 is regular Noetherian, and at every point its vanishing $t_j$ are distinct regular parameters. Thus [lem-trf-nc-coordinate-blowup-branch-drop] applies with exactly the center ideal $(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$. Using step 3, the strict transform on its $i$-th blowup chart has equation $\prod_{j\ne i}t_j^{\prime}=0$, is empty or normal crossings, and has at most $m-1$ branches; for $m=1$ it is empty. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] these give etale neighborhoods covering the points over $M$.

Over $X\setminus M$, [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] and [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement] identify $X^+$ with $X$ and $D^+$ with $D$; the charts of [lem-trf-nc-subboundary-branch-atlas] restricted over $X\setminus M$ give the local equations, and step 1 gives $b_{D^+}=b_D<m$, so $b_{D^+}\le m-1$. $D^+$ is reduced, as scheme-theoretic closure of the reduced open $D\setminus M$ [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image]. On the jointly surjective etale family formed by the step 4 charts $W\times_XX^+$ and these restricted atlas charts, the pullback of $D^+$ is empty or cut out by a product of regular parameters, a non-zero-divisor in the regular local rings, so $D^+$ is effective Cartier by [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent]. With step 4 this covers every geometric point of $X^+$.

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII 4.1.6 and 4.1.8; Lemma 4.2.9, printed pp. 118--119 and 121.

lean.statement: theorem nc_maximal_branch_blowup {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [CompactSpace X] (hX : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.affineOpens, x ∈ U.1 ∧ IsRegularRing Γ(X, U)) (B D : X.IdealSheafData) (hB : B.IsNormalCrossingsDivisor) (hDred : IsReduced D.subscheme) (hDne : Nonempty D.subscheme) (hcomponents : ∃ C : Set (Set B.subscheme), C ⊆ irreducibleComponents B.subscheme ∧ (D.support : Set X) = ⋃ Z ∈ C, B.subschemeι '' Z) : ∃ (m : ℕ) (T : Closeds X), 1 ≤ m ∧ (∀ x : X, D.ncBranchCount x ≤ m) ∧ (T : Set X) = {x : X | D.ncBranchCount x = m} ∧ (T : Set X).Nonempty ∧ (∀ z : (vanishingIdeal T).subscheme, ∃ U : (vanishingIdeal T).subscheme.affineOpens, z ∈ U.1 ∧ IsRegularRing Γ((vanishingIdeal T).subscheme, U)) ∧ (∀ x : X, x ∈ T → ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (e : W ⟶ X) (w : W), IsAffine W ∧ Etale e ∧ e w = x ∧ ∃ (d r : ℕ) (hmr : m ≤ r) (hrd : r ≤ d) (t : Fin d → Γ(W, ⊤)) (hR : IsNoetherianRing (W.presheaf.stalk w)), @IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (W.presheaf.stalk w) _ _ hR (List.ofFn (fun j : Fin d ↦ W.presheaf.germ ⊤ w (by trivial) (t j))) ∧ D.comap e = ofIdealTop (Ideal.span {∏ j : Fin m, t (Fin.castLE (hmr.trans hrd) j)}) ∧ B.comap e = ofIdealTop (Ideal.span {∏ j : Fin r, t (Fin.castLE hrd j)}) ∧ (vanishingIdeal T).comap e = ofIdealTop (Ideal.span (Set.range (fun j : Fin m ↦ t (Fin.castLE (hmr.trans hrd) j))))) ∧ (IsEmpty ((vanishingIdeal T).ncStrictTransformIdeal D).subscheme ∨ ((vanishingIdeal T).ncStrictTransformIdeal D).IsNormalCrossingsDivisor) ∧ (∀ y : (vanishingIdeal T).blowup, ((vanishingIdeal T).ncStrictTransformIdeal D).ncBranchCount y ≤ m - 1)
